# Set 44 candidate cutoff snapshot core — review draft

Prepared 2026-11-17 against committed source `17e0362244c2bd419ed30ee902887b0ece2ad268`. **Draft, not an execution or oracle approval.** This document specifies the core foundation; the separate helper/native contract must preserve its authority, bounds and lifecycle. No runtime, new golden outputs, public transactions or official league activation are authorized by this document alone.

## 1. Approved behavior and honest scope

Mike approved eligibility and condition fixed at Saturday noon Pacific, including roster membership and ownership at that cutoff. Later roster changes, transfers or retirement never change the already locked event. Mike also approved waiting for the required seed, without a substitute or automatic cancellation, with chain-incident escalation at the following Saturday noon if that seed has not finalized. These decisions are recorded in `slug/EVENT_LOCK_POLICY.md` and `slug/BRAWLCHAIN_SPEC.md:77–78`, accepted in decision-only commit `b7985449768989cd808897c9ba9a432dbdd11729`; the runtime baseline remains17e036.

This slice implements a **candidate cutoff snapshot**, for the two existing published fixture gyms, under one previously initialized immutable participant set. It fixes the historical entry selection, roster, candidate assignment facts and condition at cutoff. It does not implement transferable ownership: `ownership_basis` is always `candidate_assignment`, with the exact account authority, account, gym and stable/source evidence. D76's production ownership requirement remains an explicit activation gate for a future transferable ownership authority. Neither old admission JSON nor today's account assignment is silently promoted to that authority. Candidate snapshots can never be relabelled official snapshots.

The historical selection rule is strict: a mutation is effective for the cutoff only if its **durably retained `committed_at_ms < cutoff_ms`**. Equal earlier timestamps are ordered by each journal's operation sequence. A sampled pre-cutoff commit can finish its synchronous write after noon and still be included; a prepare or acknowledgment timestamp alone never determines inclusion. Exactly-at-cutoff roster changes are excluded. This agrees with existing entry admission's strict cutoff.

A snapshot freezes selected fighters' verified original DNA and immutable birth projected with condition v1 at exactly cutoff, XP=0 and training=0. Preserve D65/D75, all old IDs, schemas, receipts, previews and live conditions. Retirement at cutoff excludes participation; retirement later does not edit this candidate event. The separate immediate-title-vacancy rule is not changed and no title authority is implemented here.

The coordinator first exists with both participant pins fixed **before cutoff**. Its first row for a particular Saturday may be created afterward. This enables late capture after downtime without selecting participants after the fact. Initialization at or after cutoff cannot snapshot that older event. There is no extra per-Saturday preregistration rule. Both gyms must later authenticate their own capture, possibly after a fresh login. One gym's session never authorizes capture for the other. The event is incomplete until both contributions have been durably captured; unavailable history is not an empty contribution.

There is no seed authority, selected block, finality report, anchor, matchmaking, fight, result, points, training, XP mutation, transfer, fee or global event registry in this version. Only the pinned-calendar incident deadline is computed. It is not evidence that a seed is pending or a chain incident exists. A future seed authority must apply D77; the present UI may truthfully disclose that seed integration is unavailable.

## 2. New package, participant pin and calendar

New package `gymevent` owns one separate LevelDB journal. It does not own account, entry, stable, registry, wallet or node handles. It stores no credentials, seeds, scalars, source records, SVG, caller clock or signing callback.

`gymevent.Pin` contains exactly two existing validated `gymentry.Pin` values, sorted by `StablePin.Identity.GymID`, with different AccountIDs, GymIDs and stable/entry StoreIDs. The identities must be exactly `zero256` and `incrementing256`, once each. Both pins have the same account authority, entry namespace, network/genesis, entry CalendarID/RulesID, condition-v1 selector and compiled candidate descriptor. Each source authority remains individually pinned; source authorities need not be equal. Structural validation does not establish trust: the parent supplies these exact pins from its established, validated child installations under its root lock, never browser input, unsigned marker adoption or discovery.

The coordinator StoreID binds this complete Pin. Generation and view IDs do not enter it. If both trusted existing installations are already ready, parent initialization needs no live child or login. A fresh missing participant cannot be derived in advance: current AccountID and manifest AuthorityID are independently random at first login/preparation. Snapshot installation alone is incomplete until both trusted pins exist; that state must not disable existing mining, stable, entry, login or reset controls. Do not provision an unvisited account/authority just to satisfy snapshot setup. Old routes and data remain unchanged. Full installation details belong to the companion helper contract.

Reuse the exact embedded entry-calendar TZif bytes, SHA256 `200d05754f6d83a371cf408d7085125797657b3b0bebeba1e508cffe86a3e5c8`, and its existing CalendarID. Event dates remain valid canonical Saturday `YYYY-MM-DD` in 2026–2099. SourceEvent is the unchanged `gymentry.EventForDate` under either participant pin. `incident_deadline_ms` is local noon on the date seven civil days later under that same frozen zone, **not** cutoff plus a fixed 168-hour duration. The deadline-only calculation permits the following date in January 2100 (including 2099-12-26 → 2100-01-02); it does not admit a 2100 event. No host timezone or caller-supplied UTC instant enters this calculation.

New `gymentry.IncidentDeadline(event Event) (int64,error)` is a pure validated calendar helper and changes no intake encoding or rules. It first validates the original Event completely, then derives the next local Saturday noon with the pinned zone and exact round-trip date/time checks.

## 3. Normative shapes and scalar rules

Below, fields are in canonical JSON order, tags are their literal snake_case names, and every field appears. `uint32`, `uint64`, `int64`, `string`, `bool`, arrays and named existing types mean their exact Go types; no generic maps or `any`. All integers are canonical nonnegative decimal and at most their declared cap, counters also <=2^53−1. Times are positive <=8,640,000,000,000,000, except explicit zero sentinels. All IDs/digests are canonical lowercase 64-hex; optional IDs are `""`. Arrays are nonnull. No signed manifest number occurs because these core shapes retain no full manifest. Existing condition fields retain their exact current integer types/semantics.

### 3.1 Stable/entry historical seams

In `gymstable` add:

- `CutoffFence`: `version uint32=1, store_id string, cutoff_ms int64, observed_at_ms int64, operation_count uint32`. Observed time is the successful actual clock sample whose high water was synchronized, >=cutoff; operation_count is the total journal count while that store's gate was held, <=4096. This is observation evidence, not a signature or portable proof.
- `CutoffRoster`: `version uint32=1, store_id string, cutoff_ms int64, committed_count uint32, last_sequence uint64, history_digest string, revision uint64, slots [10]string, assigned_at_ms [10]int64`. Counts/time/revision reflect only committed operations before cutoff. Empty slots have assigned time0; nonempty slots have the last **changed** placement time for that slot, positive and <cutoff. A no-op does not reset placement time. Empty history has count/sequence/revision0 and all slots/times empty/zero, but its domain-separated digest is still present.
- `CutoffMember`: `slot uint32, slot_assigned_at_ms int64, assignment Assignment, class string, condition_at_cutoff fightercondition.Snapshot`. The private verified Item and full manifest/receipt remain internal to stable; none are exposed to the callback. Slot is0..10 and assigned time0 iff slot0. Members are sorted by prospect ID, <=5.
- `CutoffSelection`: `version uint32=1, roster CutoffRoster, members []CutoffMember`. This is the preflight value; the later final callback separately receives the actual durable fence.

In `gymentry` add:

- `CutoffEntry`: `version uint32=1, store_id string, event Event, entry_id string, committed_count uint32, last_sequence uint64, history_digest string, latest_receipt *Receipt`. The only nullable field is latest_receipt: null means no committed operation for this event before cutoff. A committed withdrawal is nonnull with empty members. Counts/hash include only this event's committed receipts before cutoff; other events and abandoned/prepared intents do not supersede it. Last sequence is the original global operation sequence, not a new dense event sequence.
- `CutoffSnapshot`: `version uint32=1, entry CutoffEntry, roster gymstable.CutoffRoster, members []gymstable.CutoffMember`. This transient preflight DTO contains at most the latest saved IDs, no arbitrary requested IDs.
- `CutoffFences`: `version uint32=1, stable_fence gymstable.CutoffFence, entry_fence gymstable.CutoffFence`, passed only at final commit after both observations have synchronized.
- `SnapshotSourceInfo`: `version uint32=1, store_id string, pin Pin, observed_at_ms int64` for a short authenticated metadata callback. It does not contain roster or source proofs.

### 3.2 Event journal shapes

In `gymevent` add these exact shapes:

- `Pin`: `version uint32=1, calendar_id string, rules_id string, participants []gymentry.Pin` (exactly2, sorted as §2).
- `Info`: `version uint32=1, store_id string, pin Pin, created_at_ms int64, event_count uint32`. This bounded parent-installation metadata is not account authorization, trust discovery or event contents; no clock observation/write occurs.
- `Event`: `version uint32=1, event_id string, source_event_id string, store_id string, namespace_id string, calendar_id string, rules_id string, saturday string, cutoff_ms int64, incident_deadline_ms int64`.
- `AssignmentOwner`: `ownership_basis string="candidate_assignment", account_authority_id string, account_id string, gym_id string`. These are immutable candidate assignment facts from the pinned stable authority, not a transfer ledger.
- `Member`: `slot uint32, slot_assigned_at_ms int64, assignment gymstable.Assignment, class string, condition_at_cutoff fightercondition.Snapshot, eligibility string`. Slot0 means not rostered at cutoff; class is one of `light, welter, middle, light_heavy, heavy`. Eligibility is `eligible`, `not_rostered` or `retired`; retired takes precedence if both exclusion predicates apply. All saved members remain in the snapshot with a deterministic eligibility reason; do not silently drop excluded fighters.
- `ParticipantSnapshot`: `version uint32=1, participant_id string, entry_store_id string, owner AssignmentOwner, roster gymstable.CutoffRoster, entry gymentry.CutoffEntry, members []Member`. ParticipantID equals the pinned GymID. Members are <=5, sorted by prospect ID, and exactly match latest replacement receipt IDs; a withdrawal/no committed entry yields `[]`. Roster is the complete historical ten-slot ID state, not a claim that all ten unselected fighters were independently proof-verified during this capture.
- `CaptureEvidence`: `version uint32=1, participant_id string, stable_fence gymstable.CutoffFence, entry_fence gymstable.CutoffFence, captured_at_ms int64`. Captured time is the coordinator's actual final sample, >=both fence observations and cutoff. No historical field is relabelled with it.
- `ParticipantCapture`: `version uint32=1, snapshot ParticipantSnapshot, evidence CaptureEvidence`.
- `SnapshotInput`: `version uint32=1, event Event, participants []ParticipantSnapshot` (exactly2 in Pin order).
- `SnapshotReceipt`: `version uint32=1, input SnapshotInput, snapshot_digest string, captures []CaptureEvidence, completed_at_ms int64`. Captures are exactly2 in Pin order; completion is >=both capture times. The digest commits only SnapshotInput: actual capture/completion times, total post-cutoff operation counts and current source/roster tails do not make different historical inputs. The complete receipt has its own separate evidence digest.
- `EventStatus`: `version uint32=1, store_id string, event Event, exists bool, phase string, captured_participants []string, snapshot_digest string, coordinator_created_at_ms int64, created_at_ms int64, completed_at_ms int64, observed_at_ms int64, seed_authority string="unavailable"`. Coordinator-created time is the immutable store initialization time; event-created time is the separate first reservation time. Captured IDs are in Pin order. Phase is `before_cutoff`, `awaiting_capture`, `capturing` or `snapshotted`; before_cutoff is derived for an absent row only. Absent rows have created/completed times0, no captured IDs/digest; existing rows have actual first capture-start created time. No saved row is created before cutoff. Snapshotted has both captures, nonempty digest/completion; otherwise completion0/digest empty.
- `CaptureResult`: `version uint32=1, status EventStatus, capture ParticipantCapture, replayed bool`. Replay means the exact previously retained participant capture is returned; new observation/status time may advance, but capture bytes never do.
- `HistoryPage`: `version uint32=1, store_id string, after_event_id string, next_event_id string, has_more bool, observed_at_ms int64, events []EventStatus` (<=8, sorted by cutoff then EventID). Nonempty cursor must name a retained row.

Typed validators run before final leases and must cross-check Pin/Event/participant/store/calendar/rules relations; each stable/entry cutoff has the same C; Member Assignment, class and exact projected condition agree with canonical DNA derived from WorkHash and compiled descriptor; XP=0; assignment acceptance and birth are before C. Nonzero member slot/time matches historical roster; for a rostered member acceptance <=slot placement time<C. Every member also equals its saved receipt's immutable assignment, and acceptance <=that receipt's committed time<C. Changed slot membership since entry save is allowed if it is rostered at C; retain the noon slot, not the saved slot. Full source work/authorization/receipt digest authenticity comes from the concrete callback, not from these structural validators.

## 4. Canonical bytes and hashes

Canonical JSON is UTF-8 compact encoding in the field order above and the unchanged field order of nested existing types. No optional fields, whitespace, HTML escaping, floats, exponents, -0, BOM, invalid UTF-8 or extra top-level values. Storage must already be canonical. Transport parsing may accept whitespace, key order and escaped ASCII key spelling, but rejects duplicate decoded or unknown keys, wrong primitive types and unknown arrays before populating DTO slices, then validates and canonicalizes. Max object depth12, key names64 bytes. Only the declared arrays are allowed at their exact paths and sizes. Existing unsigned conditions use their canonical types; do not widen negative-number admission globally.

`H` means SHA256; `raw32` means decoded displayed hex without byte reversal; `LP(b)=LE32(byte_length)||b`. All displayed `\0` are one NUL. Define one fixed `Rules` object in this exact order:

`{"version":1,"boundary":"committed_before_cutoff","condition_time":"cutoff","ownership_basis":"candidate_assignment","condition_version":1,"projector_id":"slug-fighter-condition-candidate-v1","xp":0,"training":0,"participants":2,"members_per_gym":5,"exclusion_order":"retired_then_not_rostered","later_changes":"immutable","seed_authority":"unavailable"}`.

- `RulesID = H("SLUG candidate snapshot rules\0v1\0" || LP(canonicalJSON(Rules)))`.
- `StoreID = H("SLUG candidate event store\0v1\0" || LP(canonicalJSON(Pin)))`.
- `EventID = H("SLUG candidate cutoff event\0v1\0" || raw32(StoreID) || raw32(SourceEventID) || LE64(C) || LE64(IncidentDeadlineMS))`.
- `SnapshotDigest = H("SLUG candidate cutoff input\0v1\0" || LP(canonicalJSON(SnapshotInput)))`.
- `ReceiptDigest = H("SLUG candidate cutoff receipt\0v1\0" || LP(canonicalJSON(SnapshotReceipt)))`.
- Stable history start `h0 = H("SLUG stable cutoff history\0v1\0" || raw32(stable_store_id) || LE64(C))`; for each committed operation with time<C in ascending original sequence, `hi = H("SLUG stable cutoff row\0v1\0" || raw32(hprevious) || LE64(sequence) || LP(canonicalJSON(existing gymstable.Operation)))`. Final h is HistoryDigest.
- Entry history start `h0 = H("SLUG entry cutoff history\0v1\0" || raw32(entry_store_id) || raw32(source_event_id) || LE64(C))`; same row fold with domain `"SLUG entry cutoff row\0v1\0"` and existing `gymentry.Operation`, selecting only committed operations for this event with time<C.

No full live journal hash, prepared row, abandoned row, current roster revision, future source count, new capture time, new capture-session generation/view or credential/nonce enters SnapshotInput. This exclusion does not strip the original public generation, view ID or operation ID already present in the retained historical entry receipt or committed history rows: those remain byte-identical original provenance and are included by the specified canonical encoding/fold. This intentionally permits post-cutoff journal growth and later resolution of old prepared intents without rewriting the locked historical input. All committed pre-cutoff no-op roster operations do enter the stable history fold, even when revision is unchanged.

## 5. Concrete source APIs and lock order

New additive, concrete APIs (all clocks/write/checkpoint seams remain private tests; no public time override):

```
// gymstable; View capability, not caller-supplied records.
func (s *Store) WithCutoffSelection(ctx context.Context, session Session,
    cutoffMS int64, ids []string,
    prepare func(CutoffSelection) (commit func(CutoffFence, func() error) error, err error)) error

// gymentry; own participant View capability.
func (s *Store) WithCutoffSnapshot(ctx context.Context, session Session,
    saturday string,
    prepare func(CutoffSnapshot) (commit func(CutoffFences, func() error) error, err error)) error
func (s *Store) WithSnapshotView(ctx context.Context, session Session,
    fn func(SnapshotSourceInfo, func() error) error) error
func IncidentDeadline(event Event) (int64, error)

// gymevent: constructor Pin is trusted explicit configuration.
func Create(ctx context.Context, path string, pin Pin) (*Store, error)
func Open(ctx context.Context, path string, expected Pin) (*Store, error)
func ResumePrepared(ctx context.Context, path string, expected Pin) (*Store, error)
func (s *Store) Close() error
func (s *Store) Info(ctx context.Context) (Info, error)
func (s *Store) Observe(ctx context.Context, source *gymentry.Store,
    session gymstable.Session, saturday string) (EventStatus, error)
func (s *Store) Capture(ctx context.Context, source *gymentry.Store,
    session gymstable.Session, saturday string) (CaptureResult, error)
func (s *Store) Read(ctx context.Context, source *gymentry.Store,
    session gymstable.Session, saturday string) (SnapshotReceipt, error)
func (s *Store) History(ctx context.Context, source *gymentry.Store,
    session gymstable.Session, afterEventID string, limit uint32) (HistoryPage, error)
func EventForDate(pin Pin, saturday string) (Event, error)
func ID(pin Pin) (string, error)
func RulesID() string
func SnapshotDigest(pin Pin, input SnapshotInput) (string, error)
func ReceiptDigest(pin Pin, receipt SnapshotReceipt) (string, error)
```

Exact codec API table: for `T = Pin`, `ValidatePin(v Pin) (Pin,error)`, `MarshalPin(v Pin) ([]byte,error)`, `ParsePin(raw []byte) (Pin,error)`. For each `T` in `Info, Event, ParticipantSnapshot, ParticipantCapture, SnapshotInput, SnapshotReceipt, EventStatus, CaptureResult, HistoryPage`, expose exactly `ValidateT(pin Pin, v T) (T,error)`, `MarshalT(pin Pin, v T) ([]byte,error)`, `ParseT(pin Pin, raw []byte) (T,error)`. These return deep-owned values. Info must match the supplied Pin exactly and does not require an event. For event-bearing values, context is reconstructed from the enclosed source-event Saturday and checked against `EventForDate(pin, saturday)`; pin is never inferred from the object itself. `SnapshotDigest`/`ReceiptDigest` use these validated canonical encodings. There is no standalone public codec for nested AssignmentOwner, Member, CaptureEvidence, CutoffFence/Roster/Selection/Entry/Snapshot/Fences/SourceInfo: they are checked as part of their enclosing typed result. In particular historical source DTOs are synchronous concrete capability outputs, not an import API. Their JSON tags/order remain normative for nested event encoding and independent tests. No future unspecified `Validate*` overload is part of this slice.

Global order: helper lane/lifetime fence → event gate → entry gate → stable gate → original account View lease → stable mutex → entry mutex → event mutex. No function acquires an outer account lease before a source/stable/entry gate. No callback reenters account, registry, stable, entry, event or helper controllers. Each preflight callback executes synchronously once, after proof work while the operation gates are held but with no account lease or store mutex. It returns either an error or one nonnil final commit callback. Preflight constructs/validates immutable data, canonical bytes, snapshot digest and conservative final-wrapper size. The returned callback executes at most once under the final original lease after fences; it performs no condition projection, manifest generation, SVG rendering or Argon work. It only checks identity/cancellation, binds the actual bounded timestamps/evidence, copies, serializes and synchronizes the prevalidated batch. Callback errors, context failures and outer lease failures cannot be swallowed.

The event store never retains source/session pointers after a call. Parent owns its lifetime; the active child lends its exact live source→stable→entry chain under the existing single lane. Close drains all event calls before its DB closes. The helper cancels/joins active event calls before entry→stable→source handles are closed/rebound; the parent event store itself remains open across those child transitions. Same-gym reopened handles are allowed only with exactly matching pinned identities. Except the deliberately metadata-only Info method, every event operation authenticates the caller's concrete matching participant, not merely the supplied Session's public fields. A valid current View from either participant can read the public event snapshot/history; Capture only fills that participant's contribution. No new account capability is required: this is automatic source-derived reconciliation under View, not user entry/roster mutation. D72 held sessions can view/capture their own historical facts; mining tokens cannot provide View.

## 6. Historical capture and fence algorithm

A capture holds the event gate while obtaining concrete entry callbacks. Its first short WithSnapshotView call validates the actual matching participant and original View, advances required clocks, and checks for an existing participant capture. If present, return its exact bytes immediately with fresh status; do not replay history, rehash source records or obtain new fences. If absent, admit/reserve the event as below, release that metadata lease and only then enter the historical source seam. The entry gate excludes all entry writers; it acquires the stable gate in the existing order, which drains real roster work. A write sampled C−1 still in flight must finish or fail/poison before replay begins. Never infer absence from a timeout or unknown reply.

1. Validate normal profile, Pin, date, context and session. Perform short original View checks before disk/proof work. Read the durable coordinator CreatedAtMS and require it<C. Observe/synchronize actual clocks under their existing rollback rules. If the coordinator's actual clock is before C, return `event_not_due` before reservation/capture. Once the coordinator has reached C, a stable/entry source observation still below C is clock disagreement: the new historical seams return their existing ErrClock, mapped to `event_clock`, and cannot capture. No new old-package or old-wire error spelling is introduced. An observed forward jump is retained, not rewound. A lower actual time than a retained high water fails `event_clock`.
2. Replay complete retained operation sequences with bounded streaming rows, checking missing/index-crosslinked/canonical rows, chronology and revisions against the current audited metadata. Stable uses every operation to validate the live chain, but folds/applies only committed times<C into the historical projection. Track slot placement times on actual changes. For every historical placement, verify the retained assignment's accepted/birth bounds <=that commit time, even if the fighter is not selected for this event. Entry validates the complete sequence/per-event revision graph, then folds only this Event's qualifying commits and retains its latest receipt. No revision-only shortcut and no filtering by Prepare time.
3. Select only that latest replacement receipt's <=5 prospect IDs; withdrawal/no entry selects none. Resolve exact retained assignments; verify each source through the existing concrete pinned ManifestStore, serially, comparing the whole immutable assignment and source-record digest. Preserve normal 256 MiB work verification and candidate descriptor/manifest/portrait binding. These source operations occur without an account lease or store mutex. Check cancellation and original View before each proof; cancellation joins the current verifier and starts no next proof. No source import or caller-supplied verdict exists.
4. Use canonical manifest DNA and original birth to project condition at **C**, XP0, without using C as a current clock sample. Require source acceptance/birth<C and <=the saved entry commit, and for rostered members <=historical placement time. Derive slot/eligibility at C. A source error, record rewrite, missing assignment, incompatible descriptor or time contradiction fails the whole contribution; it is never a deterministic exclusion or empty gym. Stable invokes its preflight callback with stripped CutoffSelection; entry adds the previously replayed CutoffEntry and invokes the coordinator preflight. This completes all pure condition/manifest validation, canonical historical input and capacity checks outside the final lease. Returning nil commit without an error is invalid and cannot mutate anything beyond observations.
5. Under the final original View lease and stable mutex, revalidate retained identities/selected assignments and replay positions, persist a fresh actual stable clock >=C, and produce StableFence for the already prepared commit closure. All stable writes precede the foreign callback. Under entry mutex, revalidate its exact projection and participant pin, sample its actual clock >=stable observation and retained entry clock, persist EntryFence and ordinary closure observation for an existing source event. Do not create a new intake event merely to fence an absent one. No stable/entry writes follow the event callback.
6. Under event mutex, recheck the same current View; sample the coordinator's actual time >=both fences and its own high water. Recheck fixed identities/cancellation and the previously validated reserved size before one synced event batch. Historical Member/Pin arithmetic was already validated during preflight; do not rerun it under this lease. Save ParticipantCapture; if it is the second, create the immutable SnapshotInput/Receipt and `snapshotted` event in the **same** batch. Before invoking any foreign commit all source clocks are durable; no final pre-write source/authority I/O follows this final check.
7. Any error from a write that may have committed poisons that store. Any cancellation/reset/outer lease error after event commit returns `outcome_unknown`, never a definite rejection. Reopen exact journals, query/replay the same Event/participant and recover the original capture. Do not create a new ID, timestamp or snapshot root to resolve ambiguity. A source fence committed without an event capture is harmless incomplete progress; retry may obtain a later observation but the same historical input. A poisoned source prevents further capture until that source is explicitly reopened/audited.

A durable clock floor of exactly C is sufficient for the strict<C rule. Later commits at C or later cannot enter the sealed past. A prepared-only pre-C roster intent may later commit >=C; it is excluded and must not be automatically abandoned/applied. No fence freezes current roster controls, source catch-up or new future entries. The source schemas and their existing metadata fields stay version1: the fence is their already-synchronous ClockMS high water, while the separate event capture retains which actual observation established it. No incompatible bucket is added to old stores.

## 7. Event lifecycle, recovery and bounded storage

Coordinator initialization first durably records the exact immutable Pin, then samples actual `created_at_ms` and synchronizes it with ClockMS in final initialized metadata. Never sample CreatedAtMS before the Pin is durable: filesystem work may cross noon. `created_at_ms` never changes after initialized metadata exists, including Open or prepared-parent recovery. Before-cutoff coordinator initialization is a trusted local retained-clock fact, not cryptographic proof of wall time. No reset/relogin silently recreates it.

First Capture after cutoff reserves an event row with state `awaiting_capture` and actual created time. That reservation is synchronized before proof work, binding deterministic Event and full Pin; it can survive cancellation. One participant capture changes state to `capturing`; both atomically produce `snapshotted`. Reserve row/state is not a claim of completed fencing. Its reservation callback is a separate short WithSnapshotView lease; release it before acquiring the historical stable gate. The final event mutation returns unknown if that reservation or capture write may have committed and its result cannot be confirmed. No abandon, replacement, deletion or automatic garbage collection exists for event captures. Repeated capture only returns the same participant bytes. New current account generation authorizes reading/reconciling old facts without rewriting their historical provenance.

Observe/History may advance actual coordinator clock, but never allocate events. Observe derives absent-row phase, including an old event whose coordinator existed too late: phase alone does not imply capture permission; the separate coordinator_created_at_ms permits exact comparison against cutoff. Read requires an already complete snapshot; incomplete returns `event_incomplete`, unknown date row returns `event_not_found`. History accepts limit1..8; empty cursor starts first, unknown retained cursor fails `event_not_found`. Observe/Read/Capture/History require original current View at disclosure; caches are owned immutable data and their current-view wrappers belong to the helper contract. Polling is cached and does not execute any core method or source work.

Disk layout is exactly marker `SLUG-CANDIDATE-EVENTS.json` plus `db/`. Marker order: `application="slug-candidate-events",version=1,store_id,pin`; canonical JSON plus one LF. Metadata key ASCII `meta` has `version,store_id,pin,created_at_ms,clock_ms,event_count`. Event rows use `e || raw32(EventID)` and canonical `{version,event,phase,created_at_ms,completed_at_ms,snapshot_digest}`. Participant rows use `c || raw32(EventID) || raw32(ParticipantID)` and canonical ParticipantCapture. Complete receipts use `s || raw32(EventID)` and canonical SnapshotReceipt. Only while initialization is incomplete, ASCII key `init` may hold exact canonical `{version=1,store_id,pin}` with a20KiB cap and no metadata/event/capture/receipt rows. Normal Open rejects any init key. No other logical key/prefix/bucket is allowed. Exact key lengths are 33/65/33 bytes. Event enumeration sorts the bounded retained rows by `(cutoff_ms,event_id)`; there is no unchecked opaque index.

Open validates the exact expected Pin/marker (bounded opened-fd regular-file and identity checks), then all raw key/value sizes/counts before decoding; unknown keys, malformed row shape, missing/crosslinked captures, invalid phase/count/digest, duplicate participant, canonical mismatch or inconsistent historical summaries fail. It validates structural historical/condition arithmetic and all hashes, **without Argon, SVG rendering or claiming source authentication**. Only capture obtained authoritative provenance from the concrete source. A complete stored receipt remains readable without rereading source proofs, as conditional durable authority evidence. Missing established marker/db/ready component refuses; partial evidence remains untouched. Create accepts an absent intended directory or a verified real empty directory only, never nonempty adoption/symlink traversal. Its exact initialization order is: write canonical marker exclusively; sync marker file and containing/parent directories; create/open the intended DB; sync the sole exact init key; sync DB and store directories; sample actual positive CreatedAtMS; atomically delete init and put initialized meta with EventCount0/ClockMS=CreatedAtMS using Sync:true; sync directories; return. No event row exists at initialization. A failure after a possible batch commit is outcome_unknown, not permission to restart with a new time.

`ResumePrepared` is only for the trusted parent's already retained `prepared` installation, using its exact expected Pin. It validates the real protected path, exact complete marker and bounded directory inventory; it recognizes only (a) that marker with an absent or real empty DB directory, (b) a complete LevelDB whose logical rows are empty or exactly the matching init key, or (c) the exact initialized complete store with EventCount0 and no event/capture/receipt rows. For (a)/(b), sync the exact Pin init before taking a fresh actual CreatedAtMS and performing the same final atomic initialization. This fresh time may make an older event ineligible; never backdate it from marker mtime or original attempted time. Case(c) reopens unchanged and preserves original CreatedAtMS. Missing/partial/wrong marker, symlink, unknown path/key, inconsistent init, incomplete meta, any event data, or mixed init+meta refuses and retains all evidence. A ready parent uses only Open and never ResumePrepared/Create. This is narrow explicit initialization recovery, not generic nonempty adoption. Open of init-only state still fails closed. Every disk error closes owned handles and reports uncertain outcome where applicable; no recursive deletion or secret reads. Close cancels and joins the actual gate holder and borrowed calls, then closes only its own DB.

Fixed bounds (bytes, including all canonical wrappers): Pin/marker16KiB; metadata20KiB (includes full Pin); Event/status2KiB; historical stable roster4KiB; historical entry36KiB; Member4KiB; ParticipantSnapshot56KiB; CaptureEvidence2KiB; ParticipantCapture60KiB; SnapshotInput120KiB; SnapshotReceipt124KiB; request8KiB; response128KiB; History page8; events256; participants2; selected members5 per participant/10 total. Stable/entry replay visits <=4096 rows each, with raw row caps8192/32768, one decoded operation at a time; no unbounded journal slice/map is introduced. Complete existing Open audits retain their current documented resource bounds. Info also takes the event gate and checks closed/poison/context state; it does not call any borrowed source or synthesize a session. Parent prepared-install recovery may adopt only the exact pinned initialized coordinator with EventCount0; a ready installation must reopen the same store and preserve CreatedAtMS, never recreate missing data. Capture performs <=5 serial source work hashes, never concurrently with the miner or another lane operation. No proof for withdrawal/no-entry. Cancellation checked before each row/proof; core accepts caller context, helper task deadline remains30s and joins current noninterruptible proof. Upper bound is bounded work, not a promise every maximum journal finishes inside30s on every device.

At reservation, count admits <=256 complete worst-case events; the maximum per-event logical rows are2KiB+2×60KiB+124KiB=246KiB. Including fixed metadata/marker, retained logical bytes stay under64MiB; physical LevelDB compaction overhead is additional and must be measured/disclosed. No dynamic row-growth debt can consume another event's completion reservation. Capacity prevents a new event reservation, never completion of an admitted existing row. The formula-only bound calculation is retained in `set44-core-shape-bounds.py` and `set44-core-shape-bounds.json`; it uses deliberately oversized scalar envelopes and is not a valid-input or outcome corpus. Before reference freeze, it must confirm these conservative JSON caps using the existing nested DTO definitions; cap changes require an explicit reviewed contract revision, not an implementation surprise.

## 8. Errors and compatibility

`gymevent` exported sentinels and strings: ErrInvalid=`invalid_request`; ErrUnauthorized=`unauthorized`; ErrForbidden=`forbidden`; ErrStaleView=`stale_view`; ErrBusy=`busy`; ErrUnavailable=`event_unavailable`; ErrCorrupt=`event_corrupt`; ErrCapacity=`event_capacity`; ErrClock=`event_clock`; ErrCalendar=`event_calendar`; ErrNotDue=`event_not_due`; ErrCreatedTooLate=`event_created_too_late`; ErrIncomplete=`event_incomplete`; ErrConflict=`event_conflict`; ErrNotFound=`event_not_found`; ErrCancelled=`event_cancelled`; ErrOutcomeUnknown=`outcome_unknown`; ErrClosed=`event store closed`; ErrPoisoned=`event write uncertain; reopen required`; ErrProfile=`event requires production PoW`.

Map old source authorization/cancellation/corruption/clock/poison failures conservatively to these fixed categories; keep `outcome_unknown` if any local mutation may have committed. Missing or corrupt expected source is unavailable/corrupt, never an empty member list. A rollback/definite error cannot reveal a payload. Hook/callback failures before event commit can be definite even if observation-only fences advanced; they do not falsely assert that an event capture committed. Distinguish that from an uncertain event batch or postcommit disclosure failure.

All mutating/source-verifying new APIs reject the cheap test PoW build before filesystem access or source work. Structural codec/calendar helpers may work with production-pinned public values in that build but cannot open/capture real identity stores. No old reader is widened to adopt the new event marker. Old stable/entry/account schemas, serialization, IDs, operation/revision counters and View/EntryManage/RosterManage meanings remain unchanged. Candidate event creation/capture never mines or modifies balances, roster, entry selections, receipts, births or source admission records.
